Onyx River Weir by Lake Vanda, Antarctica

The Onyx is the longest river in Antarctica. Most years it starts flowing in late December/early January. It flows from the sea end of the Wright Valley into Lake Vanda. Lake vanda has NO outlet. So where does the water go? It evaporates.

Lake Vanda is situated in the amazing Dry Valley Region of Antarctica.

Arrival of mail and supplies at Vanda Base, Antarctica

Vanda Base was in the Wright Valley, which is in the amazing region of Antarctica known as the Dry Valleys. This region is permanently free of snow and ice, all year round. The openning view is looking towards the Dais. 1973

Huskies at Scott Base, NZ

Huskies at Scott Base (NZ), Antarctica. 1973. The huskies were extremely friendly but they fought amongst themselves, if they got the opportunity. The black "blocks" on the ice (where the dogs are tied at the start) are mainly seal meat. There are no longer Huskies at Scott Base.

Links
www.scottbase50years.co.nz
http://bobmckerrow.blogspot.com

Distant view of Vanda Base, Wright Valley, Antarctica

Distant view of Vanda Station (also known as Vanda Base), Wright Valley, Antarctica. Followed by a pan of the Wright Valley. Taken from the lower slopes of the Olympus Range in 1973. The Wright Valley is part of the amazing Dry Valley region of Antarctica, a region that's free of permanent snow and ice year round. The pan starts looking at the Dais. Vanda Base is now closed.
